verdict_reason: The POST test proves the edit keeps every stored role and ignores posted ones, but the added no-roles check is an absence assertion that cannot fail on its own and the expected body rebuilds a named helper.

todos.issue: The added absence check expect($('form input[type="checkbox"], form input[type="radio"]')).toHaveLength(0) (lines 98-100) cannot fail on its own: any type radio or roles checkbox brings a label, which the exact expect(textsOf($, 'form label')).toEqual(ADDRESS_FORM_LABELS) on line 97 already rejects; it is the absence pattern the house rules ask to replace with an exact positive assertion
todos.fix: Must: the 'no address type and no roles' claim of SCN-INS-ADDR-003-C is proved by one exact positive assertion, and the test title says so. One way: assert the form's named controls equal exactly the nine field names (plus any hidden fields the form carries), drop the checkbox/radio count, and name the no-type/no-roles claim in the title

todos.issue: The expected update body { ...VALID_ADDRESS_FIELDS, name: UPDATED_NAME, roles: STORED_ADDRESS.roles } (lines 288-292) rebuilds VALID_ADDRESS_RECORD, which address-book-requests.js:85-88 already names as exactly { ...VALID_ADDRESS_FIELDS, roles: STORED_ADDRESS.roles }
todos.fix: Must: the test uses the shared helper's name for the stored-roles record rather than rebuilding it. One way: expect(sent).toEqual({ ...VALID_ADDRESS_RECORD, name: UPDATED_NAME })
